question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=4(x+y)\,i-3x\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,1)$ to the point $B(3,3).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i+j$ and $b=3\,i+3\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i+j)+t[(3\,i+3\,j)-(2\,i+j)] \\  & =(2\,i+j)+t(i+2j) \\  & =(t+2)\,i+(2t+1)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t+2\,y=2t+1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =4(x+y)\,i-3x\,j \\  & =4(3t+3)\,i-(3t+6)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+2)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+1)j \\  & =i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(4(3t+3)\,i-(3t+6)\,j)\cdot (i+2\,j) \\  & =4(3t+3)\cdot 1-(3t+6)\cdot 2 \\  & =6t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6t\,dt \\  & =3{t}^{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3-0 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
